bug_semantics: The Markdown and PDF evaluation-export routes checked only whether the requester could view the conversion, while build_evaluation_report() selected every non-deleted evaluation comment and serialized each comment's content and author's first name without applying the existing per-comment privacy rule. A requester allowed to view a conversion could therefore export private evaluation comments that should have been visible only to the conversion owner, the comment author, or an administrator.
flaw_origin: Commit c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f directly introduced both export routes and build_evaluation_report(). The new routes called the report builder after only conversion-level authorization, and the new builder unconditionally appended all evaluation comments. The immediate parent already had the ordinary comment-visibility policy but had neither the report builder nor the export routes, so this is a direct feature introduction rather than a later import, move, rename, refactor, or aggregate.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file commit c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f shows ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com> as both author and committer, one parent, and the complete message 'add: [MarkDown/PDF] new way to see the evaluation of a convert' with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI trailer, or other commit-object AI attribution.
evidence: The assigned first-party advisory bundle for GHSA-vrrh-vgmq-m54x/CVE-2026-73140 describes missing comment-level authorization in build_evaluation_report(), identifies CWE-862, and references direct fix 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42; its package-version fields are unavailable, so the release boundary was checked from Git tags.

numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1 git log --all --reverse --format=%H%x20%P%x20%s -Sbuild_evaluation_report -- website/web/evaluate/evaluate.py website/web/evaluate/evaluate_core.py and the corresponding -Seval_comments_raw history both first return c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f with sole parent 6cd6133775a573dd93409af9b120cbb12b647988.

The direct parent diff, git diff --unified=5 6cd6133775a573dd93409af9b120cbb12b647988 c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f -- website/web/evaluate/evaluate.py website/web/evaluate/evaluate_core.py, adds both Markdown/PDF endpoints, their conversion-only _can_view_convert() checks, the actorless build_evaluation_report(convert_id) calls, the all-comments query, and unconditional author/content serialization. Those blocks are absent from the immediate parent.

git show --format=fuller --stat --summary c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f confirms a normal one-parent commit. Although its patch also contains other feature work and dependency-lock changes, the vulnerable routes and report builder are direct additions in this commit; the reverse -S history and parent diff reject an import, move, rename, refactor, merge aggregate, or smaller public-history member as the origin. Squash decomposition is therefore not applicable.

git show --format=fuller --stat --summary 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42 identifies the one-parent privacy fix. The diff from its parent 06d408e3496fdfc31da22d7b2b427434c67eae94 passes the concrete requesting actor from both export routes, adds access.can_see_comment(), and skips each comment for which that predicate is false before serializing author and content, directly closing the disclosure.

Version-boundary checks show git tag --contains c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f --sort=version:refname returns v1.4 and v1.5, while git tag --contains 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42 --sort=version:refname returns only v1.5. git merge-base --is-ancestor c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f v1.3 exits 1. Thus v1.3 predates the flaw, v1.4 is vulnerable, and v1.5 is the first fixed release.

The only assigned primary/reviewer disagreement is marker_state. Re-running numactl --cpunodebind=1 --membind=1 git cat-file commit c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f shows human author and committer ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>, exactly one parent, and only the subject 'add: [MarkDown/PDF] new way to see the evaluation of a convert'; there are no trailers, bot identities, or AI-attribution strings.

The primary's explicit checked-and-absent ai_marker claim wins over the reviewer's null. The BIC commit object was available and inspected, so the marker state is known to be absent rather than unknown or unexamined; later commits, PR metadata, branch names, and the fix commit are excluded from attribution under the BIC-only rule.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle is complete and direct: c5d258d59530292bb17ab602d3b799373540596f created a new export path that exposed every evaluation comment after only a conversion-level check, even though a finer-grained comment privacy rule already existed. Reverse content history makes it the smallest public-history origin, its immediate-parent diff proves the mechanism absent before it, and its one-parent commit object plus direct additions reject moves, imports, refactors, and squash aggregation. Fix 5dbd19b39a61eab793586731f1a80d8c38907c42 closes that exact path by carrying the requester into the builder and applying the shared comment ACL; tag ancestry establishes v1.4 as vulnerable and v1.5 as fixed. For the marker_state disagreement, both audits reached NOT_AI but encoded the inspected absence differently: the primary recorded an explicit absent state and the reviewer used null. The primary representation is correct because the BIC object is present and its complete identity/message evidence was re-inspected; it contains no qualifying AI signal. Null would incorrectly blur verified absence with an evidence gap. With the BIC, direct parent, direct fix, release boundary, and BIC-only attribution all verified, the gate-complete verdict is NOT_AI.
